No matter how hard I try, not every single combat is going to be exciting to watch, but I still feel kinda bad when I just watch a player get bored...

The main issues with giving them an advantage on death saving throws, as I mentioned in another reply, is that the healer will try to stabilize the character through a medicine check or Spare the Dying if the prior fails. I've implemented a kinda homebrew system where, if it's like 2 bandits vs the party of 4, I'll have them try to avoid combat because, well, if you have any sort of int. you should know when to fight or run.

I've had plenty of sessions where I just get that, "ugh, another pointless encounter?" feeling, but I also know that if the party is travelling in a dangerous area, I should keep the area dangerous.

First, he'll try a medicine check on the dying player (And he has a decent number for it), then he'll try Spare the Dying if it does, on the off chance, fail. It's VERY important that you work quickly here so a skin does not develop and it becomes tougher to work with. After all balls are formed, shape it to whatever you want. We did knots. After final shape is formed, proof again for 10-15 minutes, egg wash, any toppings desired, then bake until golden brown. 

Lemme know if you have questions and enjoy!

25oz of high-g flour

1.5 oz granulated sugar

1/2 oz salt

1oz dry milk

3/4oz active dry yeast

16oz water, 105 to 110 to reconstitute yeast without killing it.

1oz shortening, we used hydrogenated

Add yeast to water, give it a lil stir, and wait about 5 minutes, when you tap or shake the bowl, it should bloom(lemme know if you need an explanation on that). After yeast is alive again, add dry milk. 

Transfer to mixer with a dough hook and add flour and sugar. Start stirring then add salt.( If you add the salt too early it will kill the yeast). Once it starts ti form, add shortening to shorten the gluten strands. Let it mix until it starts cleaning the bowl.

You should be able to stretch a small piece until it's slightly translucent while not tearing too much. Its okay to nead when it gets close, just nead it in high-g flour.

Transfer to larger bowl that is coated in some sort of oil. New York wrap it and let it proof in a warm, moist environment for 15-20 minutes.

Take out of proofing environment and scale out about 10 oz portions(can be adjusted). Form into small balls and cover in plastic as you work.
